claims: A mistaken Denver Police "All Clear" emergency alert was sent citywide on Saturday, April 18, 2026.
The mistaken Denver Police "All Clear" emergency alert was sent instead of only to the immediate area of West Gunnison Drive and South Zuni Street.
The Denver Police "All Clear" emergency alert followed a robbery.
Denver7 and CBS News reported a subsequent shelter-in-place order.
The incident occurred near the southwest Denver intersection of W. Gunnison Dr. and S. Zuni St.
Two armed robbery suspects fled into a nearby residence.
Two armed robbery suspects fleeing into a nearby residence prompted a localized shelter-in-place order for a one-block radius.
After both suspects were apprehended, the "All Clear" alert was intended only for that neighborhood.
The "All Clear" alert was sent to the entire city.
This was the second incident this year where a localized emergency alert was accidentally sent citywide in Denver.
Denver Police and Denver 911 are currently investigating the cause of the alert system failure.
